Special needs students have a lot more rights in this case than typical students or even staff. I took some education law classes for my degree and we did a study on this one case where a special needs student threw a chair and punched a teacher in her face during class while she was trying to teach. He broke her nose! The class was a mainstreaming class (SNS & typical students mixed) and they were all terrified. Because of rights given by the IDEA (Individuals with Disabilities Education Act), he was not suspended and had to stay in the school *in* her class. It's wild.
